title: Jonah and the Provision
premise: Wendell Galloway has spent three years drifting between dig sites, outrunning the memory of her father Elias Galloway, the celebrated archaeologist who chose a discovery over her mother's deathbed. When rival archaeologist Marguerite Voss hires Wendell's crew to excavate the Wadi al-Nakhl — the site Elias swore off after it destroyed his marriage and his reputation — Wendell takes the job to control what gets found. Beneath the wadi she uncovers not treasure but evidence that Elias's 'fraudulent' find was real, and that Voss intends to bury the proof and salvage her own career with it. Torn between duty to her crew's contract and love for the father she's never forgiven, Wendell smuggles the truth out before the dry season seals the valley, exposing Voss at the season's final symposium and choosing, for the first time in years, to be seen.
about_author: Xanthe Coldharbour is the pen name of a former field surveyor who traded transit maps for manuscripts and now writes adventures set in the world's loneliest latitudes. She lives somewhere between two time zones with a dog named Compass and an unhealthy collection of broken compasses.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. On a roadside dig in Turkana, Wendell measures her life in distances traveled rather than time lived, establishing her exile from her father and her gift for reading ground no instrument can match. Emotional beat: restless avoidance dressed up as freedom.

chapters.title: The Letter with No Return Address
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A contract arrives from Marguerite Voss — her father's old rival — naming Wadi al-Nakhl, the one site the Galloway family swore off forever. The money would save her crew's insolvent season. Emotional beat: dread disguised as opportunity.

chapters.title: Crew of the Unattached
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet her found-family crew: pragmatic foreman Odile, superstitious young surveyor Tam, and medic Ravi who keeps everyone's secrets. They vote to take the job; Wendell hides why it matters. Emotional beat: belonging she doesn't believe she deserves.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The convoy crosses into the borderlands, and Odile observes how Wendell goes quieter with every mile toward the wadi, recognizing the look of someone driving toward a grave. Emotional beat: loyalty shadowed by worry.

chapters.title: The Valley That Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. First sight of Wadi al-Nakhl: wind-carved cliffs where her father's career ended twenty years ago. Her hands shake setting the first survey stake. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through muscle memory.

chapters.title: Voss's Terms
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Marguerite arrives by helicopter, all charm and fine print: exclusive publication rights, sealed finds, a clause forbidding contact with any Galloway. Wendell signs anyway. Emotional beat: ambition curdling into something colder.

chapters.title: First Cut
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Opening trenches yield ordinary shards until Tam's auger strikes cut stone far below the dated stratum — older than anything Elias was accused of faking. Emotional beat: wonder edged with fear of what it implies.

chapters.title: What Elias Buried
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In a collapsed side gallery, Wendell finds her father's abandoned 1998 field journal hidden in a niche — his notes insisting the find was genuine, and a page torn out. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Sandstorm Protocol
chapters.summary: Ravi's POV. A three-day storm traps the team in the tents; tempers fray, secrets leak, and Ravi patches both a broken arm and a broken confidence. Emotional beat: forced intimacy cracking Wendell's armor.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Reconstructing the missing page from water-stained fragments, Wendell learns Elias hid the original artifacts — deliberately — to keep them from Voss, who once falsified data against him. Emotional beat: fury at her father softening into terrible understanding.

chapters.title: Voss Watches
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Marguerite, tipped off by a bribed porter, realizes Wendell has found the cache and accelerates her timeline: strip the site early, ship the artifacts under her own permits, erase the Galloway name entirely. Emotional beat: cold calculation meeting rising panic.

chapters.title: Night Survey
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Wendell leads a secret night excavation of the true cache chamber while Voss sleeps; Tam keeps watch, terrified, and sees Wendell weep over her father's handwriting on the wall. Emotional beat: devotion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Sealed Chamber
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The chamber opens: intact artifacts, inscriptions vindicating Elias completely — and evidence Voss's mentor committed the actual fraud decades ago. Emotional beat: vindication arriving too heavy to carry alone.

chapters.title: Confession at the Fire
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Wendell finally tells her crew everything — her name, her history, what they're really holding. Instead of anger, they offer to help her get it out. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility paid and refunded in trust.

chapters.title: Clause Seventeen
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss invokes the contract's penalty clauses, threatens the crew's licenses, and orders the site locked down with hired security. Wendell appears to capitulate. Emotional beat: the trap closing with legal precision.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Clock
chapters.summary: Ravi's POV. Weather reports confirm the pass road closes in nine days; Voss's shipment leaves in six. The crew plans a decoy manifest and a mule route through the canyon while Ravi quietly treats Wendell's worsening altitude sickness. Emotional beat: hope rationed like water.

chapters.title: Decoy
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The crew runs a false loading operation while the real artifacts travel by night with Odile; Tam is caught covering tracks and refuses to give names under Voss's interrogation. Emotional beat: courage discovered in the least likely person.

chapters.title: Canyon Run
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell escorts the final crates through flash-flood country as the season's last storm breaks early; a near-drowning forces her to choose saving the artifacts or saving Tam, and she chooses Tam — the artifacts float free in their sealed case. Emotional beat: love outbidding duty at last.

chapters.title: What the Valley Kept
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss seizes the decoy crates, celebrates prematurely, and discovers the forgery planted inside — Wendell's counterstroke. Enraged, she files fraud charges against Wendell and heads to the symposium to control the narrative. Emotional beat: hubris sprinting ahead of its own collapse.

chapters.title: Symposium
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the season's closing symposium, Wendell presents the authentic provenance chain, the recovered journal, and testimony from her crew, dismantling Voss publicly and clearing Elias's name. Emotional beat: the invisible woman stepping fully into the light.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Her father, aged and unwell, waits outside the hall having followed the controversy for years. Their reconciliation is awkward, unfinished, honest — he asks nothing except to see the valley again through her eyes. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a door left open, not a debt erased.

chapters.title: Homecoming Miles
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew drives back north together, Wendell navigating by choice now rather than flight, planning a return expedition with Elias invited. She still counts miles — but each one now leads somewhere. Emotional beat: belonging earned, journey continued.
